summary: This note summarizes the highest scoring Premier League games and biggest winning margins since the league's establishment in the 1992-93 season. It highlights Manchester United's 9-0 win over Ipswich Town as the record biggest win. It also covers Tottenham Hotspur's 9-1 win over Wigan Athletic, which holds records for goals in one half, and Manchester United's 8-1 away win at Nottingham Forest.
one_line: A summary of the Premier League's highest scoring games and biggest winning margins since 1992-93, led by Manchester United's 9-0 win over Ipswich Town.
key_facts: The Premier League was established in the 1992-93 season, the starting point for this list of highest scoring games.
The record for the biggest win in the Premier League is Manchester United's 9-0 victory against Ipswich Town.
Manchester United's 9-0 win over Ipswich Town took place at Old Trafford on 4th March 1995.
Tottenham Hotspur are the only other club to have scored nine goals in a Premier League game.
Tottenham Hotspur won 9-1 against Wigan Athletic at White Hart Lane on 22 November 2009.
The Tottenham 9-1 Wigan game set a record of nine goals scored by both teams in one half of Premier League football.
The Tottenham 9-1 Wigan game set a record of eight goals scored by one team in one half of Premier League football, achieved by Tottenham.
Manchester United hold the record for the biggest winning margin away from home.
Manchester United won 8-1 away against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground in Nottingham on 6 February 1999.
